mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever found yourself searching for peace in the middle of all the noise and hurry of daily life? Sometimes, it feels almost impossible to slow down and just breathe, doesn’t it? But what if there was a gentle space, an invitation to step away from the rush and discover a quiet kind of reassurance that meets you right where you are? That’s what we get to explore together through Jesus Calling: Enjoying Peace in His Presence, crafted by Sarah Young. In these pages, you’ll find more than just words—you’ll discover a soft place where anxieties begin to loosen their grip, and the idea of a loving, divine presence feels suddenly possible. Here, comfort isn’t found in grand gestures, but in those small, everyday moments when you turn inward and listen for encouragement and guidance. Rather than chasing after peace in the world around us, we’ll see how it can actually be found within, through a relationship that brings hope no matter what season we’re in. As we move through this journey, each day becomes a gentle invitation—to pause, reflect, and recognize the sacred woven into the ordinary. There’s no pressure to strive or achieve; it’s about opening up, letting grace meet you right where you are, and noticing how acceptance, gratitude, and surrender can gently reshape your outlook. Together, let’s discover how peace isn’t some far-off dream, but a reality waiting right here, ready to be welcomed into our lives.

Chapter One: Discovering Stillness in a Restless World
Picture this: the day barely starting, and already your mind is sprinting ahead—chasing after all the emails, family needs, and that never-ending pressure to get things done. Sound familiar? For most of us, mornings can feel like a blur, a rush to keep up. But underneath all that noise, there’s often this quiet longing for something more. Not just survival, but a real sense of calm. Maybe even the feeling that life is more than just a to-do list—that it’s actually a journey with meaning.
And you know what? You’re not alone in feeling this way. People everywhere are searching for peace—a kind that doesn’t disappear when life gets tough. Some of us try to fill the emptiness by staying busy, or by reaching for distractions, but that restlessness? It lingers. The real invitation here is simple: pause. Listen. Notice that peace isn’t about escaping trouble, but about discovering something deeper, something greater, right in the middle of it all.
Imagine a woman, sitting quietly at her kitchen table. The house is still, her coffee’s gone cold, and for once, she doesn’t reach for her phone. She’s learned, after many anxious mornings, that these first few moments can shape her entire day. So she closes her eyes, takes a slow breath, and lets the silence settle in. In that gentle quiet, she feels a kind of reassurance—a reminder that she’s not alone, that there’s a presence beside her, offering comfort and guidance.
This simple act—making space for stillness—becomes her lifeline. It’s not about running away from reality. Instead, it’s about rooting herself in something deeper that’s always there, even when the outside world feels out of control. Within this quiet space, there’s a calm that doesn’t get shaken by whatever’s happening around her.
Over time, she realizes this peace isn’t something she has to earn. It’s not an achievement—it’s a gift. Freely given, always waiting. The real challenge? Not to try harder, but to let go. To stop gripping so tightly for control, and just trust that there’s a loving presence guiding each step forward.
And here’s something you might notice when you practice this stillness: bit by bit, your worries lose some of their power. Decisions feel less overwhelming. Even when life gets tough, there’s this quiet sense—you’re not facing it all alone.
Now, don’t get me wrong—it’s not a one-time breakthrough. Some days, finding that peace feels easy. Other days, it’s a struggle. But the invitation is always there: come back. Return, again and again, to that quiet center where assurance and hope live.
In time, this journey toward peace becomes more than just a personal quest. It shapes the way you live. Ordinary moments turn into chances for connection, for renewal. And step by step, you start to find that, no matter how restless the world gets, stillness is always within reach.

Chapter 2: Building a Personal Connection with Jesus
As each day goes by, the idea of having a personal relationship with Jesus starts to shift—it moves from something you just believe in, to something you can actually feel and experience.
For a lot of us, faith might start out as a collection of lessons or family traditions—things we’re taught, or maybe things we just pick up over time. But eventually, it hits you—what really keeps you going isn’t just knowing about God. It’s the sense that you’re part of an ongoing, honest conversation.
Picture this: a young professional, totally swamped by the pressures of a new job, starts to feel lost. She’s heard people say that prayer is more than just repeating words, but honestly, she’s not sure how to begin. One tough evening, she sits down quietly and just opens up—she shares her fears, her dreams, even her confusion. There’s no booming voice of reply, but in the stillness, she feels something gentle—a sense that she’s been heard, that someone gets what she’s going through.
That story? It’s not unique. It happens in so many lives. When you turn inward, speak honestly, and then simply listen, you’re opening the door to a relationship that’s both deeply personal and incredibly comforting. And here’s the thing—it’s not about saying the right words or following a perfect script. It’s about being real—bringing your true, sometimes messy self into the conversation.
Over time, something amazing happens. This relationship grows deeper. The happy moments become chances to say thank you, and the tough moments become invitations to lean in, to trust a little more. People often notice subtle shifts—maybe challenges don’t feel quite so lonely, or decisions are made with a sense of guidance and support that wasn’t there before.
Take, for example, a parent juggling work and family, running on empty by the afternoon. She’s about to lose her patience, but instead, she pauses—takes a deep breath—and quietly asks for help. The answer isn’t always instant or obvious, but there’s a new sense of strength, a quiet feeling that she’s not on her own. It helps her choose kindness over frustration.
This kind of ongoing dialogue isn’t just for the big, dramatic moments. It’s woven into everyday life—whether you’re walking to work, doing dishes, or just waiting in line. Every little moment is a chance to check in, to listen, to share what’s on your mind. And honestly, the relationship grows not through grand gestures, but through those small, steady acts of attention and openness.
For so many people, this personal connection becomes their anchor—it’s what keeps them steady when life gets stormy. It’s a wellspring of comfort, wisdom, and hope. And maybe the most beautiful part? It’s a reminder that you are seen, you are known, and you are loved—not because of what you achieve, but simply because of who you are.

Chapter 3: Trusting Through Uncertainty and Hardship
You know, life almost never goes exactly the way we’d hoped. Plans get derailed, and challenges appear out of nowhere—maybe it’s an illness, a loss, disappointment, or just unexpected change.
When things get tough, it’s so easy to slip into fear, or try to grab control of every little detail. But here’s the thing: it’s often in those seasons of uncertainty, when we feel most lost, that we’re given the greatest chance to trust.
Picture this—a man suddenly loses his job. Anxiety hits hard. The future looks like a massive question mark, and the weight of providing for his family feels heavier than ever. He’s always seen himself as self-reliant, the kind of guy who handles whatever comes his way. But now, his usual approach just isn’t working.
In the quiet of an evening, he remembers something simple, but powerful: every worry, big or small, can be brought into an honest conversation with Jesus.
So, he starts to share his fears, not hiding his frustration or confusion. And as he opens up, he begins to sense a gentle reassurance—a reminder that he isn’t defined by his situation, and most importantly, he’s not alone in facing it.
Does the path ahead get clearer? Not right away. But there’s this growing trust, this feeling that he’ll be guided, one step at a time.
Surrendering like this isn’t easy. It goes against the urge we all have to fix, to plan, to control. Yet, letting go doesn’t mean giving up. In fact, it’s about opening yourself to a strength bigger than anything you could muster on your own. It’s believing that, even in the hardest moments, there’s both purpose and presence working behind the scenes.
Now, imagine a college student facing massive uncertainty about her future. She’s always been a planner—setting goals, working hard, ticking boxes. But suddenly, her path is anything but clear, and every option feels risky.
In a moment of quiet, she decides to let go of her desperate need for certainty. She asks for guidance and for peace. The answer doesn’t show up as a detailed roadmap. Instead, she finds a quiet confidence—a gentle assurance she won’t have to walk alone, no matter which direction she chooses.
What becomes clear over time is that trust isn’t just a one-and-done choice. It’s a daily practice. Some days, trust flows naturally. Other days, it takes real effort. But every single act of surrender brings a little more freedom—a sense of relief from having to control every single outcome.
And here’s something truly powerful: as people learn to trust, they often become more resilient in tough times. Setbacks stop feeling like failures, and start looking like chances to grow in faith and reliance. The journey will still have pain, but it’s also filled with a deeper hope—a belief that, even in the darkest moments, light can still be found.

Chapter 4: The Power of Gratitude and Presence
You know, in the rush of daily life, it’s so easy to miss the little gifts that show up in each day.
Our minds naturally zoom in on what’s missing, what’s wrong, or what needs fixing. But if you really pause and look closely, you’ll notice that every single moment is sprinkled with reasons to feel grateful—simple joys, unexpected kindness, and those quiet moments of beauty that so often slip by unnoticed.
Picture this: a retiree, just settling into a new, slower rhythm of life, suddenly finds herself feeling a bit empty. The days feel long, unstructured, and a little too quiet. So, one afternoon, she puts on her shoes and heads out for a walk. This time, though, she decides to really pay attention—to the warmth of the sun, the sound of children’s laughter, the gentle breeze against her skin. As she names these small blessings, something shifts inside her. The emptiness fades, replaced by a quiet fullness—a realization that even in the simplest moments, there’s so much to be thankful for.
Practicing gratitude doesn’t mean you’re ignoring pain, or pretending everything’s perfect. Instead, it’s about choosing to focus on what’s good, even when things are tough. It’s a way to gently retrain your mind, helping you notice the presence of God—or whatever you call it—in the ordinary, everyday stuff.
Take a teacher, for example. She’s worn out from the demands of her job, feeling stretched thin. So, she tucks a little notebook into her bag and makes a promise to jot down just three things she’s grateful for each day. Some days, her list fills up fast. Other days, she really has to hunt for even the smallest blessing. But over time, she notices something powerful: her outlook starts to shift. The challenges are still there, but they don’t feel quite so overwhelming. Gratitude becomes her anchor, something steady she can hold onto in the present moment.
What many people discover is that gratitude and presence go hand in hand. When you’re lost in the past or worrying about the future, it’s so easy to miss the gifts right in front of you. But when you bring your attention back to the here and now, even the most ordinary moments can become sacred.
Of course, this kind of shift doesn’t happen overnight. It takes intention, practice, and plenty of patience. But as gratitude settles in as a habit, you start to notice a deeper sense of peace and joy bubbling up. It becomes clear—the presence of God, or whatever gives your life meaning, isn’t only found in special occasions or dramatic moments. It’s woven into every single day, quietly waiting for you to notice and receive it.

Chapter 5: Hearing God’s Voice in Everyday Life
You know, the idea of hearing God’s voice can seem mysterious—maybe even a little intimidating.
Have you ever wondered if it’s really possible, or thought maybe it’s just something reserved for a select few?
As you walk this journey, though, something shifts. You start to realize that this kind of communication isn’t just possible—it’s actually personal, and it’s open to everyone.
Picture this: a nurse working long, exhausting shifts in a busy hospital. She’s surrounded by constant needs and the pressure never seems to let up.
Still, she decides to carve out just a few minutes each day to sit quietly and listen, letting her heart open up.
At first, all she notices is the noise in her head—distractions, doubts, endless to-do lists.
But slowly, something changes. She begins to sense subtle nudges—a wave of calm when she’s making a tough call, a gentle feeling she should check on a struggling coworker, or a quiet confidence in the middle of fear.
These moments? They aren’t loud or dramatic.
They arrive as whispers, gentle impressions, or just a deep-down sense of knowing.
And here’s the thing: the more you practice listening, the more you start to catch these quiet signals.
It’s not about hearing actual words out loud. It’s about noticing how God speaks—maybe through a verse that sticks with you, the beauty of a sunrise, the kindness of someone you meet, or a sudden stillness in your heart.
Take another example: a student facing a major life decision.
She spends some time reflecting and honestly asking for guidance. The answer doesn’t show up right away, but over the next few days, she starts to feel a sense of clarity growing inside her.
A chat with a friend, a line in a book, even a rush of unexpected peace—all these moments seem to point in the same direction.
It’s like guidance comes in bits and pieces, woven right into the fabric of everyday life.
This whole process takes patience and a willingness to stay open.
It’s so easy to miss that quiet voice when life gets noisy and distracting, isn’t it?
But the more attention you give to listening, the stronger your ability to discern becomes.
A lot of people find that keeping a journal really helps—just jotting down thoughts, impressions, or little moments, and then looking back to see patterns or answers that weren’t obvious right away.
Over time, it becomes clear: hearing God’s voice isn’t about having some special technique or secret formula.
It’s all about relationship. Being willing to listen, to wait, and to trust.
Sometimes, what you hear might not be what you expected, but it’s always rooted in love, wisdom, and peace.
Ultimately, this journey is about more than just getting answers.
It’s about deepening your connection—finding meaning in each day as you listen, respond, and grow closer to the One who’s always present, always speaking, and always inviting you in.

Chapter 6: Surrendering Control and Embracing Dependence
You know, there comes a moment in almost every life when that sense of control... just slips right through your fingers. Maybe it’s a sudden diagnosis, a relationship you thought would last, or a dream you quietly watched fall apart. The instinct is to fix it—to manage, to force a solution. But as the days go by, it hits you: some things just can’t be forced into place, no matter how hard you try.
Picture a father—someone who’s always been sure he could provide and protect. Now, bills are mounting, his child’s struggling in school, and the future feels more uncertain than ever. He does everything he can to keep it all together, but the weight keeps growing. Then one night, when the house is finally quiet, he sits in the dark and whispers to himself, “I can’t do it all.” It’s terrifying, but there’s also this strange sense of freedom.
In that quiet moment of surrender, something actually changes. He starts to realize that being dependent isn’t a sign of weakness—it’s an entryway to a deeper kind of strength. Letting go of the urge to control every outcome? That takes real courage. It’s not about just giving up or checking out—it’s about trusting that he doesn’t have to carry the load all alone.
For many of us, surrender isn’t just a one-time thing; it’s a rhythm we learn. Every morning brings fresh worries and that old temptation to chase after certainty. But each time you release your grip, you might notice a little more peace, a gentle reminder that life isn’t meant to be managed solo. Dependence—something you might’ve feared—can quietly become your source of confidence.
Now, think about a business owner watching her company slip away. She’s grieving, she’s angry, she’s asking all the hard questions. But as she starts to let go of her plans and expectations, something unexpected happens. Friends show up with meals, a new opportunity appears, and she realizes her worth isn’t measured by her bank account or business card. The journey is still tough, but she’s not carrying it by herself anymore.
Over time, it starts to make sense—surrender isn’t about giving up, it’s about giving over. It’s handing your messy, complicated life into the care of something loving and steady that’s always at work. The freedom you find isn’t about never struggling again. It’s about knowing that, even in the middle of the struggle, there’s real hope.

Chapter 7: Finding Hope in the Midst of Darkness.
You know, darkness can sneak into our lives in so many different ways—grief, depression, disappointment, or fear. It’s kind of like a heavy blanket that settles over everything, smothering joy and making even the smallest tasks feel impossible. Have you ever felt that way? Where hope just seems out of reach, like a tiny light barely visible at the edge of your world?
Imagine a widow, waking up each day to an empty house after decades of sharing her life with someone. The silence is almost too much, and the ache never really lets up. She moves through her routine in a bit of a haze, not quite sure how to keep going. One rainy afternoon, she sits by her window, just watching the drops slide down the glass. She remembers when hope used to come easily—when faith was something simple, not a distant memory.
But as the days roll by, little things start to stand out. Maybe a neighbor offers a wave. Maybe a letter shows up from an old friend. Or maybe she spots the first crocus poking through the last of the snow. These small moments don’t erase her pain, but they do offer a glimpse of something more. She starts writing in a journal, jotting down every little mercy, every act of kindness that comes her way. And you know what? Bit by bit, hope returns—not like a sudden explosion, but as a gentle companion, quietly sticking with her as she walks through her darkness.
Or think about a teenager, tangled up in anxiety. Nights are the worst. Worries pile up, and sleep feels miles away. One night, instead of trying to push the fear away, he just whispers a simple prayer for help. The anxiety doesn’t magically disappear, but suddenly, he doesn’t feel so alone. There’s a gentle presence, almost like someone sitting with him in the dark.
The thing about hope is, it’s not really something you can force. For most of us, it’s more like a gift—something that shows up in small, unexpected ways. Maybe it’s the kindness of a friend, the beauty of a sunrise, or just that quiet feeling that darkness isn’t the end of the story.
Over time, it becomes clear: hope isn’t about pretending pain doesn’t exist. It’s about having the courage to believe that pain isn’t all there is. It’s choosing to look for light, even when the path forward isn’t clear. In the end, hope becomes a lifeline—a thread that ties where we are right now to a future that’s still unfolding.
So, if you’re sitting in darkness today, remember—you’re not alone, and hope is closer than you might think.

Living with Open Hands: Generosity and Compassion.
As your journey deepens, you might notice a new invitation appearing—the chance to live with open hands. You know, it's natural to want to protect what feels limited. Maybe it's your time, your energy, your resources, or even your love. We hold on tight, thinking there's not enough to go around. But here's something surprising: the more we give, the more we actually receive.
Imagine a single mom, busy with work and parenting, barely holding it all together. One day, she sees her neighbor struggling with heavy grocery bags. She hesitates—her schedule is packed, and honestly, she's exhausted. But something inside her nudges her to reach out and help. The neighbor’s gratitude is instant, and as they chat, she realizes her own worries feel just a little bit lighter. That simple act of giving, of stepping outside her own troubles, brings her an unexpected joy.
Or think about a retired teacher, living on a tight budget. She decides to volunteer at a local food pantry. At first, she wonders if she has anything left to offer. But as she listens to the stories of the people she helps, her heart opens up. Just showing up, offering kindness and her presence, brings her a sense of meaning and connection she didn’t see coming.
Generosity isn’t just about money or things. It’s about your attention, your willingness to listen, and making space for someone else. It’s choosing compassion instead of judgment, and being present instead of distracted. What’s amazing is, the more you practice generosity, the less you feel like you’re missing out. That old sense of scarcity starts to fade. You realize life isn’t a zero-sum game—there really is enough love, enough grace, and enough hope for everyone.
Over time, living with open hands can become your way of life. Sure, there are days when you just want to pull back and protect yourself. That’s completely normal. But each act of compassion, every small moment of generosity, is like planting a seed in the soil of your soul. The harvest doesn’t always come right away, but it’s real—deeper relationships, more joy, and a sense of purpose that goes way beyond your circumstances.

Chapter Nine: Transformation Through Daily Practice
Change... it almost never happens overnight, does it? More often, it’s the result of those small, steady choices we make—tiny habits that slowly shape our hearts and minds. If you’re hoping for more peace and presence in your life, that journey is really built one day at a time, through simple practices that anchor your soul.
Imagine a young artist struggling with self-doubt. She decides to give herself just ten quiet minutes every morning. She lights a candle, opens her journal, and lets the words spill out—whatever’s on her mind. Some mornings, the thoughts come easily; other days, she sits in silence, a little uncertain. But, as the weeks go by, something begins to shift. Her anxiety softens, her creativity starts flowing again, and she feels more connected—to herself, and to God.
Or think about a grandfather, long retired. Every morning, he takes a walk around the neighborhood. It’s his time to pray, to notice the changing seasons, maybe to wave hello to a neighbor or two. The routine isn’t complicated, but it grounds him. He finds his days are calmer, his patience grows, and his heart feels more open.
Here’s the thing—these daily practices aren’t about getting it perfect or putting on a show. They’re really about showing up, again and again, with honesty and openness. Some days, it might feel like nothing’s happening. Other times, you might stumble onto an unexpected insight or a bit of comfort you didn’t know you needed. Over time, all those small moments add up, slowly transforming every part of your life.
What’s surprising is that the most powerful practices are often the simplest: things like gratitude, a few minutes of silence, a prayer, or a small act of kindness. There’s no secret formula—just a willingness to come back, day after day, to whatever helps you find peace.
And as those habits take root, you’ll start to notice the change isn’t just personal. It ripples outward. Families become more patient, workplaces feel a little kinder, neighborhoods grow more connected. That ripple effect? It starts with the quiet, daily choice to seek presence and peace—one small step at a time.

Chapter 10: Abiding in Peace—Living the Invitation
Let’s talk about what it really means to live out this invitation to peace. You know, as our journey unfolds, peace becomes less of a finish line and more of a way we show up in the world. It’s not just for those rare, perfect moments or spiritual highs. It’s there in the mess of a busy morning, in the quiet when you just can’t sleep, and in the uncertainty that comes with every new beginning.
Think about a couple who’s been married for decades. They’re facing the changes that come with getting older—health challenges, shifting plans, and a future that feels a little less certain than before. But as they lean into being present and trusting each other, something beautiful happens. They find a new closeness. Suddenly, they laugh a bit more, they forgive a little quicker, and they savor the small joys that each day brings. Peace, for them, isn’t about everything being easy—it’s really about love showing up, even in the tough moments.
Or picture a recent college graduate, stepping out into the unknown world of adulthood. She’s carrying with her the lessons of stillness, gratitude, and trust. She knows hardships will come. Plans are bound to change. But she also knows she’s not on this path alone. The simple practices she’s learned become like a compass, guiding her through uncertainty with hope and courage.
For a lot of us, abiding in peace isn’t about checking out of life or escaping the world. It’s about showing up—fully, and with all our imperfections. It’s about trusting that grace is enough, even when things feel overwhelming. Living with open hands, open hearts, and open eyes. Ready to receive, ready to give, and open to being changed in the process.
The journey isn’t over. There’ll be days when you doubt, when everything feels like a struggle, when peace seems just out of reach. But the invitation is always there—come back, again and again, to that quiet center inside yourself, where love and assurance never really leave.
In the end, life becomes a kind of prayer—a daily practice of trust, gratitude, and hope. That’s the real invitation: to keep returning, to keep abiding, and to let yourself be shaped by peace, right in the middle of real life.

As we wrap up our time with Jesus Calling: Enjoying Peace in His Presence by Sarah Young, I want you to remember—this journey isn’t about finding some secret formula for a perfect life. Instead, it’s an open invitation to slow down, to trust a little deeper, and to open your heart just a bit wider each day. The stories and gentle guidance in these pages remind us that peace isn’t something you have to chase. It’s something you can receive—sometimes right in the middle of your everyday, ordinary moments. So, as you head into whatever comes next, keep these gentle truths close: Stillness? That’s a choice you make each day, not just once and for all. Honest conversations with God bring real connection and quiet reassurance. Trust gets stronger the more you’re willing to let go and lean in. Being grateful and truly present can turn even the simplest days into something sacred. And when you give generously or show compassion, your heart opens to even more joy and meaning.
There’ll be days when peace feels far away, when trust is hard, and gratitude seems out of reach. That’s normal. What matters is your willingness to pause, to listen, and to try again. Every small step—every moment you surrender or choose presence—moves you forward. Just know, you’re never walking this path alone. The invitation to peace is always open—waiting for you in the quiet, in the chaos, and in those gentle nudges of love throughout your day. So, take a deep breath. Let go of what you can’t control. And trust that you’re being held, even now. The journey keeps unfolding—and with every step, you’re growing into someone who carries peace, not just for yourself, but for the world around you. Keep going.
